learning_outcomes.statement: The learner can decompose a project into small testable steps, apply incremental development with pre-planned test scenarios, and use a systematic expected-vs-actual debugging workflow.

The learner can build at least 16 small integrated programs combining strings, numbers, conditions, loops, and collections from Chapters 1-11, and can articulate the data-vs-algorithm (refactoring) principle.

reviewers.attestation: Read scripts/build_chapter_12.py in full (all lesson-builder functions), cross-checked every printed/claimed code result by executing the corresponding snippets under the project's own .venv (Python 3.14.6), ran every canonical notebook for this chapter via scripts/run_notebook.py, independently re-verified every grader's expected value, and confirmed the canonical source and review-surface sha256 values match the current committed state exactly.

criteria.rationale: Two defects were found and fixed during this batch: F-010 (MINOR, a stale cross-reference pointing to a section that does not contain the referenced bug pattern) and F-011 (MAJOR, three factually wrong numeric/string claims clustered in one 'deterministic' terminal transcript); every other claim across all 16 projects was independently re-executed under Python 3.14.6 and confirmed correct.
All arithmetic, string, loop, and collection behavior across all 16 projects verified against the actual Python 3.14.6 interpreter.
Precise terminology (декомпозиция, рефакторинг, MVP) introduced with genuinely worked, verified examples rather than bare definitions; register entries added for both.
The opener promises project methodology plus 16 named integrated projects across text/data/graphics categories; all delivered with no gap once the two content defects were fixed.

All grader-relied-upon claims (statistics, quiz scores, journal/cart totals, polygon angles) independently re-executed and match exactly; the corrected text-analyzer transcript now matches its own project's pre-existing, already-correct grader values (12-11.py/12-12.py).
Concrete, checkable scope (16 named projects, each with a stated goal) rather than vague aspirations.
Explicitly and correctly attributes each project's constituent skills to their origin chapters (1-11), assuming nothing not already taught.
Explicitly reframes 'project' vs 'exercise' via a comparison table before any project code, grounding the chapter's purpose before its content.

16 sections chunked into a clear rhythm (methodology -> text projects -> data projects -> graphics projects -> closing synthesis), each following the same 5-stage project template established at 12-07.
12-06's closing recap (16-project tree diagram, capability map, Chapter-1-to-12 growth comparison) and its evidence-based bridge to Chapter 13 functions provide genuine, well-grounded consolidation.
Terminology used identically across all 16 projects; correctly reuses rather than restates concepts from Chapters 5-11.
All internal section cross-references verified against the chapter's own numbering scheme; the one stale cross-reference found (F-010) has been corrected.

The counter/accumulator-reset-inside-loop bug is deliberately and explicitly reused as a running motif across three Debug Labs (12-08's origin, 12-09, and 12-14 after the F-010 fix), each correctly citing its predecessor rather than re-deriving the bug independently.
Chapter number, title, and all 16 section identifiers match the PAGES navigation model and sidebar exactly.

Every behaviorally checkable claim across all 16 projects (arithmetic, string processing, quiz scoring, journal/cart totals, polygon angles) independently re-executed under the project's .venv Python 3.14.6.

decision.rationale: Full canonical source read end to end, all 22 notebooks executed and all 20 graders independently re-verified, two confirmed defects (F-010, F-011) found and fixed; no blocker/major/minor findings remain open; ready for the human subject_matter_reviewer, methodology_reviewer, and final_approver gate required before APPROVED.
